name: Product summary
pitch: Create a one-page summary of a product for new sales reps.
instructions: Start by reading the person's product description from their workspace with file_read. If no file exists, ask the person for the text or a link. Open a browser tab and navigate to any public pages about the product, such as a website or docs, using browser_navigate. Use browser_snapshot to read the page content. If the page has a product description, copy the key points. If not, search the web with web_search for the product name and read those results. Collect all facts about what the product does, who it is for, and what makes it different. When you have enough information, close unnecessary tabs with browser_back. Open make_page and create a single-page document that has a short intro, a bullet list of the main features, a sentence on who it is for, and a sentence on why it is useful for sales reps. Save the page as 'product-summary.md' in the workspace with file_write. If any step finds nothing, say plainly what could not be found and stop. When the page is ready, show it to the person with show_table or a short message so they can decide whether to keep it.
starters: make a quick overview for reps

examples.ask: summarise my product for new sales reps
examples.does: reads the product description from the workspace, browses the website, and makes a one-page summary saved as a file.

readme:
# Product summary

Create a one-page summary of a product for new sales reps.

What it does: reads the product description from the person's workspace, browses the web for extra details, and writes a single-page document with the key points, target user, and sales value.

What it needs: browser tools to read web pages, make_page to create the document, and file_read to get existing notes.

What it will not do: it cannot write the summary without existing product text or web information, and it will not publish or send the file without the person's say-so.
